key_insight: TRACER predicted future diagnoses across external health systems; at 95% specificity, flagged patients were up to eight times more likely than unselected patients to receive a diagnosis within one year.
clinical_relevance: EHR-based risk prediction could support disease screening, but detection rates and false-alert burden varied by disease and health system.
method: Pretrained a decoder-based foundation model on longitudinal EHRs from over 4.5 million patients across four health systems.
Evaluated 16 incident diseases at 1-, 2-, and 5-year prediction horizons.
Assessed screening performance at low false-positive rates, beyond global discrimination metrics.
evidence_signal: External evaluation included more than 2 million patients from two health systems excluded from development, with discrimination retained across systems.
watch_item: Stable discrimination did not ensure consistent detection or false-alert burden, highlighting the need for local evaluation before screening use.
paper_title: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems
